items.prompt: In n8n, what flows between two connected nodes?
options: An array of items, each a JSON object — most nodes run once per item by default
A stream of raw HTTP responses
items.explanation: Items are the unit of dataflow; the per-item default execution is the fan-out that surprises everyone with N expensive-node calls for N items. (obj-05-a)

items.prompt: Why do workflow exports never contain credentials?
options: Credentials live encrypted in a separate store and are referenced by name — the canvas and the key store are deliberately separated
Credentials only exist on the n8n cloud plan
n8n strips them for size reasons
items.explanation: The separation is a safety property: exports can be shared, versioned and committed while secrets stay in the encrypted store. (obj-05-a)

items.prompt: Reading an execution as an operator, what is the most efficient way to locate the incident?
options: Re-run the workflow and watch live
Walk the canvas in data-flow order and find the FIRST node whose output diverges from what you expected
Read every node's output top-to-bottom until something looks odd
items.explanation: The divergence-hunt is the operator's core skill: the first node whose emitted items surprise you is the phase where the loop misbehaved. (obj-05-b)

items.prompt: What makes an n8n execution 'auditable by default'?
options: Every run records status, timing and per-node input/output data — the runtime keeps its own receipt of what happened
Executions email the owner a summary
items.explanation: The recorded per-node I/O is n8n's built-in account; the system's decision receipts layer argument on top of the raw record. (obj-05-b)
